The following process is applied to each positive integer: the sum of its digits is subtracted from the number, and the result is divided to 938 is 102, since 938−(9+3+8) = 102. Applying the process twice to 938 the result is 11, ap9 plied three times the result is 1, and applying it four times the result is 0. When the process is applied one or more times to an integer n, the result is eventually 0. The number obtained before obtaining 0 is called the house of n. How many integers less than 26000 share the same house as 2012?
